A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPSA research work. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic matrix-sensing experiments, including comparisons with ScaledSM, parameter sensitivity and a rebalancing ablation.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 report original Gaussian-map and matrix-sensing experiments. Appendix A.4 additionally reports OPSA results on two real video datasets.

M1.justification: V2 removes the explicit nuclear-norm/factor-norm penalty, the lambda-L and lambda-R update terms, and Algorithm 2's rebalancing procedure. Lambda remains in the preconditioners, while the Polyak step uses the unpenalized objective. These change the proposed method, although v1 already omitted rebalancing in most experiments.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian matrix sensing only. V2 adds partially observed video background subtraction on shoppingmall and restaurant, extending evaluation to real data and robust matrix completion. It also evaluates additional corruption levels.

E2.justification: ScaledSM remains the matrix-sensing comparator. V2 Figures 8–9 add AccAltProj foreground/background decompositions as qualitative references. AccAltProj uses rank 2 and full observations, whereas OPSA uses d = 10 and 30% observations, so this comparison has different input conditions.

E3.justification: The corresponding sensing comparisons change kappa from 5 to 20, lambda from 25/50 to 2, and the d/r grid from 1.4–3.0 to 1.0–2.6. The lambda sweep and displayed iteration horizons also change substantially. Appendix A.4 introduces evaluation with 30% video observations and fivefold rank overestimation.

E4.justification: V2 removes the rebalancing ablation and substantially revises lambda sensitivity testing. It adds condition-number sweeps up to 10,000, outlier-density tests at 1%, 5%, 10% and 15%, and an empirical Gaussian-map RIP illustration. These investigate several previously untested robustness and theoretical questions.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 4 explicitly reports 95% confidence intervals over 20 trials; that experiment and its uncertainty reporting disappear. V2 Figure 1 documents 500 random trials for the new Gaussian-map illustration. These counts concern different experiments, and v2 supplies no corresponding confidence-interval protocol for its optimization comparisons.

E6.justification: V2 adds conditioning, corruption-density, Gaussian-map and video-recovery results, and replaces the corresponding overparameterization and lambda curves. V1 reports possible stalling at large lambda; v2 reports slower linear convergence at its tested extremes. Because the method and settings change, these are new or replaced findings rather than demonstrated same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The alignment metric changes from orthogonal Q to general invertible Q with inverse-transpose alignment of R. Restricted sharpness changes from rank at most 2d to rank at most d. Theorem 5.4 revises initialization requirements and its contraction constant from 0.15 to 0.12 under different hypotheses. Matrix-sensing sharpness, outlier bounds, iteration complexities and substantial appendix derivations are also revised.

C1.justification: V1 presents explicit variational nuclear-norm regularization and acceleration from imbalanced initialization as contributions. V2 removes those contributions and emphasizes unpenalized OPSA, its revised distance metric and convergence analysis. Its abstract explicitly claims rank-independent linear rates, while the broader robust asymmetric recovery objective remains.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies condition-number-independent convergence by noting that initialization requirements worsen with conditioning. It discusses unavailable optimal loss values for Polyak steps and the different RIP requirements of matrix completion. V1's explanations connecting regularization to sharpness and initialization imbalance to acceleration are removed, substantially revising the account of mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 provides a specific Matlab repository, CPU/RAM information and replacement download links for the video datasets. Matlab 2024a remains unchanged. V1's explicit initialization scaling c = 3 is no longer documented; this omission does not establish a changed experimental initialization.

R1.justification: V2 removes the dedicated variational nuclear-norm/global-optimality discussion and associated literature, including its reliance on Ding and Wang for sharpness results. It adds Charisopoulos et al. for sensing conditions, Goffin for step schedules, and a substantive LoRA connection through Zhang and Pilanci. This changes the paper's research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, conclusion and theoretical exposition are substantially rewritten. Experiments are reorganized into separate overparameterization, conditioning, lambda and corruption discussions. The appendix's known-rank discussion is integrated into the main analysis, and v2 adds an Impact Statement and a new experimental appendix.

P2.justification: V2 adds RIP, conditioning, corruption and video displays, removes the rebalancing figure, and redraws existing comparisons with revised legends and axis ranges. Table 1 is substantially compressed, Algorithm 1 is redisplayed in the appendix, and the document adopts a different conference layout. These are extensive visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical breadth, code/data access information and applicability qualifications, but a new central proof gap prevents a reliable net assessment. V1 uses orthogonal alignment; v2 allows general invertible Q yet retains lambda I in the transformed update immediately after Eq. (46). Algorithm 1 instead transforms that term to lambda Q^{-1}Q^{-T}, requiring additional justification for the claimed contraction. The expanded experiments do not resolve this theoretical issue.
